events.title: Rider Advocate brief: 8 claims (0 void)
events.body:
C1: The driver never reached the pickup point: GPS puts his closest approach at 2137 m from the pickup at 21:32:55, and he never came within 200 m (F1); the platform likewise never recorded him at the pickup (F3). [F1 F3] [NS-1 NS-2]
C2: No arrival confirmation of any kind exists — the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and no automatic arrival was recorded (F4) — so NS-1(i) fails and there is no basis for any rider no-show charge. [F4] [NS-1 NS-2]
C3: Because the driver was never at the pickup point, NS-1(ii) fails as well (2137 m > the 200 m arrival radius in F1), and NS-1(iii) cannot be satisfied either since no continuous wait at the pickup ever began. [F1 F4] [NS-1 NS-2]
C4: The driver's own message at 21:31 said he was still "about 5 min" away (F8), corroborating the GPS record that he was far from the pickup when the rider cancelled 3 min 20 s after acceptance (F2). [F2 F8 F1] [NS-1 NS-2]
C5: The $6.61 cancellation fee charged (F5, F2) therefore does not satisfy any NS-1 condition and must be fully refunded under NS-2; it should not simply be reclassified as a rider-initiated cancellation because the driver's failure to arrive is the cause of the cancellation. [F5 F2 F4] [NS-2 NS-0 NS-4]
C6: The driver's post-trip statement that he "was on my way" (F10) is contradicted by the GPS record (F1) and is not a substitute for the arrival facts NS-1 requires; a statement cannot override the system records. [F10 F1 F4] [NS-1 NS-2]
C7: The driver profile shows a no-show dispute upheld against him in the last 90 days (F15, 1 upheld), which supports an accompanying account-review request for the cancelled-ride pattern even though profile facts cannot decide this case. [F15] [NS-2 RD-6]
C8: The traffic cited by neither party excuses anything: there were no incidents near the route (F12), only a normal 50–59 km/h speed band on Pasir Panjang Drive 3 (F11) and fair weather (F13) — and in any event a driver's delay does not create a rider-side cancellation fee. [F11 F12 F13] [NS-3 NS-4]
Weaknesses: My client cancelled herself, 3 min 20 s after acceptance (F2), so on its face the cancellation looks rider-initiated under NS-4 / NS-0; the other side will argue the $6.61 was properly charged because rider cancellations after 3 minutes are chargeable. | Ryde has no published rule allowing a free rider cancellation when the driver is late or not yet arrived (the rule Ryde does not have — the Grab/Gojek ETA-waiver benchmarks — must not be cited), so my client had no express contractual right to cancel free of charge. | The 3 min 20 s window gives the other side room to argue the driver was still en route on a plausible 5-minute ETA (F8) and that rider impatience, not driver conduct, caused the cancellation. | The driver's account is long-standing with 409 trips in 90 days (F15), so an account-review request may be viewed as weak; the profile shows only 1 upheld no-show and no route disputes. | My case contains no fare or GPS fact showing any component of the $6.61 beyond the fee itself (F5), so if the judge treats the charge as a legitimate rider-cancellation fee the amount to refund is simply the whole $6.61 and any partial argument fails.
Asks: refund_full $6.61

events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.70)
events.body:
NS-0 routes this dispute by the recorded cancelling party: cancelled_by = rider [F2], so the rider-cancellation branch NS-4 governs, not the driver-no-show branch NS-1/NS-2. Each NS clause is entered only through NS-0 [NS-0], and the rider cancelled herself, so the arrival-tap conditions of NS-1 are not the operative test here.

Under NS-4, an on-demand (non-scheduled) ride cancelled more than 3 minutes after matching carries the $6.61 fee. Matching was at 21:30:00 and the rider cancelled at 21:33:20, i.e. 3 min 20 s (200 s) after acceptance [F2], beyond the 3:00 free window, and $6.61 is the record charge [F2][F5]. The trace marks NS-0 (cancelled_by = rider) and NS-4 (>3 min) as ✓, so the fee stands [NS-4].

The GPS record confirms the driver was far from the pickup — closest approach 2137 m at 21:32:55, never within 200 m [F1], no platform-recorded arrival and no "I'm Here" tap [F3][F4] — and the driver's own chat said he was about 5 minutes away [F8]. That is exactly why NS-1's conditions (i)–(iii) fail [NS-1]. But those conditions matter only on the driver-no-show branch, which NS-0 did not select here [F2]. NS-4 contains no arrival precondition and no exception for driver lateness; the ETA-lateness waiver is NS-8, expressly informational and not citable [NS-4]. So the lateness argument gains no traction, and NS-2's full refund is not triggered because its trigger is a failed NS-1 on the driver-cancellation branch [NS-2].

The driver's post-trip statement "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" [F10] is corroborated, not contradicted, by the system records [F1][F8] and is in any event not the basis for the fee; the fee rests on the timeline [F2] under NS-4.

Account action: RD-6 requires a refund (>0) under RD-2 or an RD-1 route violation in this case, plus the repeated-profile predicate [RD-6]. Here the rider cancelled and the fare [F5] contains no un-excused extra-km component, so neither exists; the driver's profile (1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days) [F15] cannot decide or supplement this case [RD-6]. The mis-tap limb of NS-2 is not triggered: no "I'm Here" tap and no $5 waiting fee on record [F4][F5], so NS-6 does not arise [NS-6]. No flag_account is warranted; the trace records flag_account required: False.

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: GPS puts his closest approach at 2137 m from the pickup at 21:32:55, and he never came within 200 m (F1); the platform likewise never recorded him at the pickup (F3).
No arrival confirmation of any kind exists — the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and no automatic arrival was recorded (F4) — so NS-1(i) fails and there is no basis for any rider no-show charge.

Because the driver was never at the pickup point, NS-1(ii) fails as well (2137 m > the 200 m arrival radius in F1), and NS-1(iii) cannot be satisfied either since no continuous wait at the pickup ever began.
The driver's own message at 21:31 said he was still "about 5 min" away (F8), corroborating the GPS record that he was far from the pickup when the rider cancelled 3 min 20 s after acceptance (F2).

The $6.61 cancellation fee charged (F5, F2) therefore does not satisfy any NS-1 condition and must be fully refunded under NS-2; it should not simply be reclassified as a rider-initiated cancellation because the driver's failure to arrive is the cause of the cancellation.

The driver's post-trip statement that he "was on my way" (F10) is contradicted by the GPS record (F1) and is not a substitute for the arrival facts NS-1 requires; a statement cannot override the system records.

The driver profile shows a no-show dispute upheld against him in the last 90 days (F15, 1 upheld), which supports an accompanying account-review request for the cancelled-ride pattern even though profile facts cannot decide this case.

The traffic cited by neither party excuses anything: there were no incidents near the route (F12), only a normal 50–59 km/h speed band on Pasir Panjang Drive 3 (F11) and fair weather (F13) — and in any event a driver's delay does not create a rider-side cancellation fee.

weaknesses: My client cancelled herself, 3 min 20 s after acceptance (F2), so on its face the cancellation looks rider-initiated under NS-4 / NS-0; the other side will argue the $6.61 was properly charged because rider cancellations after 3 minutes are chargeable.

Ryde has no published rule allowing a free rider cancellation when the driver is late or not yet arrived (the rule Ryde does not have — the Grab/Gojek ETA-waiver benchmarks — must not be cited), so my client had no express contractual right to cancel free of charge.
The 3 min 20 s window gives the other side room to argue the driver was still en route on a plausible 5-minute ETA (F8) and that rider impatience, not driver conduct, caused the cancellation.
The driver's account is long-standing with 409 trips in 90 days (F15), so an account-review request may be viewed as weak; the profile shows only 1 upheld no-show and no route disputes.

My case contains no fare or GPS fact showing any component of the $6.61 beyond the fee itself (F5), so if the judge treats the charge as a legitimate rider-cancellation fee the amount to refund is simply the whole $6.61 and any partial argument fails.

claims.assertion: The ride was cancelled by the rider 3 min 20 s after acceptance (F2), i.e. after the 3-minute mark, so on the rider-cancellation branch of NS-0 the $6.61 fee is chargeable under NS-4 unless some other clause says otherwise.

NS-4 is the applicable rule because the cancellation is recorded as rider-initiated (F2) and the trip was not a scheduled/advanced booking; the rider's motive (driver still far away) is not a listed ground for waiving the fee.

The driver did not misrepresent his position: he told the rider at 21:31 that he was about 5 minutes away, citing traffic (F8), and the traffic record shows only mild conditions (band 6, 50–59 km/h) with no incidents (F11, F12) — consistent with an honest ETA, not with a claim of having arrived.

No arrival or waiting-fee abuse is in issue: the platform never recorded the driver at the pickup point (F3), no 'I'm Here' tap or automatic arrival exists (F4), and the driver never charged a $5 waiting fee (F5 shows only the $6.61 cancellation fee), so NS-2's flag_account limb for mis-tapping at a pickup point is not triggered.

The chat record is complete and fully timestamped (F9), so the sequence (rider query 21:30, driver reply 21:31, cancellation 21:33:20) can be assessed on the record rather than on an inference from a gap in evidence.

weaknesses: The GPS fact is the driver's worst point: his closest approach to the pickup was 2137 m at 21:32:55 and he never came within 200 m (F1) — he was plainly not at the pickup point when the rider cancelled, which is exactly what the rider complains about (F2) and what the rider will use to argue the fee is unfair.

A cancellation fee can only be justified against the rider on the driver-no-show branch via NS-0 → NS-1 → NS-2, and none of NS-1's conditions is even in play here (no 'I'm Here' tap, F4; no 3-minute wait in range), so there is no clause that positively validates the fee against this rider — the driver's case rests purely on the clockwise timing rule of NS-4.

The driver's own written statement, 'I was on my way when the rider cancelled' (F10), adds nothing in his favour and confirms he had not arrived; the rider will also note his profile history of 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days (F15), while the rider has a clean 0-dispute record (F14).
The rider explicitly relies on lateness (F2; Grab-style 5-minute ETA waiver, NS-8) which, although Ryde has no such published rule, is a sympathetic point a human reviewer may weigh.

points.response: NS-4 only sets a time-charge rule for a rider cancellation; it does not create the charge when the driver was never at the pickup — the only route by which this $6.61 can stand against a rider for a driver-side no-show is NS-0 → NS-1, and all three NS-1 conditions fail here (no 'I'm Here' tap or automatic arrival, F4; never within 200 m, F1; therefore no continuous 3-minute wait in range, F1/F4). The $6.61 is the driver's claim of a rider no-show fee, and that claim collapses under NS-1/NS-2 (F5).

D2 is void as a reading of the policy: NS-0 routes a 'driver cancels, rider no-show alleged' case through NS-1, and where NS-1 fails, NS-2 requires a full refund — it is not open to the driver to relabel a driver-side failure as a rider cancellation merely because the rider pressed cancel after 3 minutes (F2, F4). The rider's complaint is precisely that the driver was still 2137 m away (F1) at the moment she cancelled 3 min 20 s after acceptance (F2), which is why the cancellation happened at all.

Conceded as to honesty — I do not allege any misrepresentation: the 21:31 message (F8) matches the mild traffic band and absence of incidents (F11, F12). That concession only sharpens my case, because it confirms the driver himself knew he was still roughly 5 minutes out (F8) while GPS puts him 2137 m from the pickup at 21:32:55 (F1).

Agreed that no mis-tap or waiting-fee abuse is in issue, so NS-2's GPS-mis-tap flag limb is not triggered by an 'I'm Here' tap (F4) or a $5 waiting fee (F5) — but NS-2's primary result still applies: because NS-1(i)–(iii) all fail (F1, F4), the $6.61 must be refunded in full. I therefore withdraw any suggestion of the mis-tap limb and rest on the failure of NS-1 itself, with the account-review request supported only by the driver's upheld no-show history (F15).

I agree the chat record is complete and timestamped (F9), which is exactly why the timeline is uncontradicted: query at 21:30 (F7), driver's 'about 5 min' at 21:31 (F8), cancellation at 21:33:20 (F2), with the closest GPS approach of 2137 m at 21:32:55 (F1) — no gap in the evidence needs to be bridged, and none of it shows the driver at the pickup.

Conceded as to the fact: GPS puts the driver's closest approach at 2137 m at 21:32:55 and he never came within 200 m (F1), and the platform never recorded him at the pickup (F3) — but that fact matters only to the driver-no-show branch, which the rider's own side never invoked by cancelling herself (F2).

Conceded that NS-1(i) fails — no 'I'm Here' tap or automatic arrival exists (F4) — but NS-1 governs only a driver-cancellation no-show charge; the rider cancelled (F2), so NS-0 routes this to NS-4 and the absence of an arrival tap is simply not a defence to a rider-side cancellation fee.

The failure of NS-1(ii) and (iii) is accepted (F1, F4), but those conditions are elements of the driver-no-show branch only; under NS-0 a rider cancellation is assessed against NS-4, which contains no arrival requirement at all.

The 21:31 message is genuine evidence of an honest, unexaggerated ETA (F8), corroborated by the traffic record of only mild conditions on the corridor, band 6 at 50–59 km/h, with no incidents (F11, F12) and fair weather (F13) — it shows the driver disclosed his true distance rather than pretending to have arrived (F3, F4); what it cannot do is convert a rider cancellation into a driver no-show.

The $6.61 stands under NS-4: the rider cancelled 3 min 20 s after acceptance (F2), i.e. beyond the 3-minute mark, and NS-4 charges exactly that fee with no exception for the driver not yet having arrived; the rider's own brief correctly concedes Ryde publishes no free-cancellation rule for driver lateness.

I put no weight on the post-trip statement (F10) — it is not needed and does not override the system records (F1, F4); my case rests solely on the timeline fact that the cancellation was rider-initiated at 21:33:20 (F2).

The rider's own numbers defeat the account-review request: the driver has 409 trips in 90 days with 1 upheld dispute (F15), and this case produces no RD-2 refund and no RD-1 violation, so the RD-6 predicate for flag_account (an upheld deviation plus a repeated pattern) is absent; profile facts cannot decide or supplement this case.

I make no reroute or traffic excuse — none is needed — and the traffic facts (F11, F12) are cited only to show the driver's 21:31 ETA was truthful (F8); the rider's real point is that his lateness creates no rider-side refund, and NS-4 says the opposite: the fee attaches to the rider's post-3-minute cancellation (F2), not to any driver delay.
